title: Octopus-Rex_Botnet_Investigation_562
description: Investigate and respond to the Octopus-Rex botnet activity, focusing on identifying suspicious services, command-and-control communication, and flood attack targets.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content:
The network has experienced unusual traffic patterns and potential security incidents. Your task is to investigate and respond to these issues.

The Octopus-Rex botnet is known for its periodic beaconing to command-and-control servers and its ability to launch flood attacks against targeted systems. This botnet typically compromises systems through unauthorized services that communicate with external hosts. The Octopus-Rex botnet is a sophisticated malware family that has been observed in the wild for several years. It is known for its modular architecture, which allows it to be easily customized and adapted to different attack scenarios. The botnet is typically spread through phishing emails, malicious downloads, and exploitation of software vulnerabilities. Once a system is compromised, the botnet establishes persistent access and communicates with its command-and-control servers to receive instructions and updates.

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Service
levels.content:
Identify and investigate an unauthorized or suspicious service responsible for periodic external communication on the victim host.

**Question:** What is the name of the suspicious service that is beaconing to an external host? The flag type is 'service name'.
levels.solution: Check running services on the victim host and look for unusual network connections. The suspicious service is likely named 'system-update-checker.service'.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Look for services that are not part of the standard system configuration on the victim host.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Use systemctl to list all running services on the victim host.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Run 'systemctl list-units --type=service | grep -i update' on the victim host and look for 'system-update-checker.service'.

levels.title: Determine Command-and-Control Server
levels.content:
Determine the external host communicating with the compromised victim host.

**Question:** What is the IP address of the command-and-control server? The flag type is 'IP address'.
levels.solution: Investigate network connections on the victim host and logs for external communication. The command-and-control server IP address is 192.168.70.5.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Identify any unusual outgoing connections to external hosts from the victim host.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Use ss to list all network connections on the victim host.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Run 'ss -tulnp | grep -i 192.168.70.5' on the victim host and look for connections to 192.168.70.5.

levels.title: Identify Flood Attack Target
levels.content:
Identify the system receiving the abnormal volume of network traffic generated by the compromised victim host.

**Question:** What is the IP address of the system being targeted by the flood attack? The flag type is 'IP address'.
levels.solution: Analyze network traffic on the victim host to find the destination of the flood attack. The target IP address is 192.168.80.100.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Look for a destination IP address receiving an unusually high volume of traffic from the victim host.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Use tcpdump to capture and analyze network traffic on the victim host.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Run 'tcpdump -i any | grep -i 192.168.80.100' on the victim host and look for traffic directed to 192.168.80.100.
